clue.text: Wobble-arse Nadir

parts.note: to wobble is to rock from side to side
bottom is a politer word for the backside

explanation.surface: A rude nickname for someone called Nadir, as if he waddled.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like an insult aimed at the fugitive tycoon Asil Nadir, a Private Eye regular; in fact it is two words to swap for synonyms plus a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest possible point of anything is its nadir, an idiom for the absolute worst level.

clue.text: Tone felt peculiar nursing hard political stance like this?

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the jumble holds the next letter
peculiar means odd, so the letters of tone felt are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at a hard-line political position that strikes someone as strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble of TONE FELT holds H for hard. The 'like this' points to the clue reading as a left-wing view.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the left means holding socialist or progressive views, a position on the political spectrum.

clue.text: Giving the castle a seizure is what Di liked to do!

parts.note: the keep is the main tower of a castle
a fit is an epileptic seizure

explanation.surface: Princess Diana enjoying giving a castle a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is Princess Diana, famous for her gym visits; the castle hints at the royal family's alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was well known for her daily exercise sessions at the gym, so exercise was her habit.

clue.text: Rows about ending of piss artist circle

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole string is read backwards
the ending of piss is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word piss
RA stands for Royal Academician, a British artist
the letter O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Quarrels over the end of a drunk's social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss artist' is British slang for a drunk, but the phrase splits: one letter from piss, and the artist is RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Here rows is the verb pronounced to rhyme with goes: someone who rows a boat oars it.

clue.text: Old rockers and the French girl shag and everything

parts.note: The Who are a 1960s rock band
le is French for the
she stands for a girl
bang is crude slang for having sex, like shag

explanation.surface: Ageing rock stars and a French girl getting up to everything at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the entire lot of something, all of it.

clue.text: Right-wing pressure group's "back to work time" getting some stick

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the group is the pieces that follow

parts.note: Monday is when the working week resumes
a club is a heavy stick

explanation.surface: A right-wing lobby's back-to-work policy getting flak.
explanation.walkthrough: The Monday Club is a Conservative pressure group on the party's right wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monday Club is a long-standing hard-right ginger group attached to the Conservative Party.

clue.text: Screw gets head replaced for a dollar

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for screw is swapped for a different letter

parts.note: vulgar slang for having sex, the four-letter word starting with F

explanation.surface: A crude remark that a screw can be had cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter comes in; the definition and the shape of the swear word make it B.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck is American slang for one dollar.

clue.text: "I can't be bothered with employment" — head

parts.note: blow it, an exclamation of not caring
a job is employment

explanation.surface: A shirker's motto about work, signed off by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the boss, but here it is slang for oral sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving head is vulgar slang for oral sex, so head is a crude synonym.

clue.text: "Gut-ache" Gada ffi possibly in charge

parts.note: Colonel Gaddafi of Libya, so his rank, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Libya's leader Gaddafi, in charge, giving everyone a stomach ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe pain in the abdomen, a form of stomach pain.

clue.text: Patriotic figure shows way to get stuffed; England's first to get shoved in

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: the letter is pushed inside the word for overeating

parts.note: to gorge is to eat until stuffed

indicators.note: England's first means the opening letter of England

parts.note: the opening letter of England

explanation.surface: A patriotic symbol is told rudely to get stuffed, with England pushed in for good measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get stuffed' looks like an insult but is a plain synonym for eating too much.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint, the dragon-slayer on the national flag, is a figure of patriotic pride.

clue.text: Idiot Ken's last to abandon London's fiasco with Tube closure

indicators.note: a fiasco is a mess, so the letters are jumbled
the letter leaves the city's name, abandoning it

parts.note: the city name taken as written

indicators.note: Ken's last means the final letter of the name Ken

parts.note: the name Ken, Mayor of London

indicators.note: the closure of Tube is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word Tube

explanation.surface: Ken Livingstone, London's mayor, quitting over a Tube shutdown fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken is Ken Livingstone, then Mayor of London and responsible for the Tube; only his final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal British slang for a silly or foolish person, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Will the impenetrable columnist take heroine from the rack?

indicators.note: taking something away removes it from the word
names the word for rack as the one the letter leaves

parts.note: a rack for storing things is a shelf
H is drug slang for heroin, the extra E making the surface

explanation.surface: Asks whether a writer famous for dense prose will grab a heroine off the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: Will Self is a novelist and columnist known for his dense vocabulary and his past heroin use, which makes the heroine pun apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer Will Self's surname is the answer; the definition names him by first name and reputation.

clue.text: Opening of curly mound pressed against tool — tawdry!

indicators.note: the tool's word is set right up against the mound's word
the opening of curly is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word curly
a heap is a mound or pile
a jack is a tool for lifting cars

explanation.surface: A tacky image of a curly heap with a tool pressed against it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapjack means of poor quality and showy, so it is a synonym for tawdry.

clue.text: Jiggling Evita's tits — journey to foreign parts for Blair?

definitions.text: journey to foreign parts for Blair

indicators.note: things that jiggle move about, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A leering line about Eva Peron's chest, then a jump to Tony Blair's travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister's official trip abroad to a foreign head of state is a formal one.

clue.text: Tony's half into Attlee, jumping on the wagon

indicators.note: into means this piece goes inside the jumbled letters
jumping means moving about, so the letters of Attlee are mixed

parts.note: the first half of the name Tony

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's side is dropped into an Attlee comparison, leaping onto a sober wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was a postwar Labour prime minister; TEETAL, the jumble of ATTLEE, holds TO. To be on the wagon is to have given up drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teetotal never drinks alcohol, which is what being on the wagon means.

clue.text: Wannabe journo is kissing Beckham's butt — that's art!

indicators.note: kissing means the pieces touch, set side by side

parts.note: a cub reporter is a trainee journalist
taken as written
the butt, or tail end, of Beckham is its final letter

explanation.surface: A trainee hack sucking up to David Beckham passes it off as art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kissing Beckham's butt' sounds like toadying, but it only joins two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism is an early twentieth-century movement in painting, so it is an example of art.

clue.text: Tabloid attack resulting from "Phew What a Scorcher!""?

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a stroke is a sudden attack of illness

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about the heat leading to a tabloid attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phew What a Scorcher!' is the classic Sun headline for a hot day.
explanation.definitionFit: Too much exposure to hot weather causes heatstroke, the illness brought on by a scorching day.

clue.text: What shows nations' positions on Taliban's initiative, finally?

indicators.note: in a down or across entry, one piece comes on, next to, the other

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps showing where countries are

indicators.note: Taliban's initiative is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Taliban

explanation.surface: A question about mapping the world's response to a Taliban initiative.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when something long awaited happens at the end, an exact idiom for finally.

clue.text: One like Milosevic, reportedly in charge of tart

indicators.note: reported speech is heard, so the words count for how they sound

parts.note: Slobodan Milosevic was a Serb

explanation.surface: A war criminal said to be running a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' is not a prostitute here but the adjective meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic means sharp and sour in taste or manner, a synonym of tart.

clue.text: Shagging traditionally on the menu at Christmas?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: vulgar slang for having sex

definitions.text: traditionally on the menu at Christmas
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the savoury filling cooked in the Christmas turkey

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings are the same word: crude slang for sex, and the sage-and-onion filling served with roast turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for having sex and also the bread-crumb mixture packed into a roast bird.

clue.text: One with itchy fingers, no stranger to G strings

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a petty thief or fraudster who cheats
second meaning: a violinist, whose instrument has a G string

explanation.walkthrough: G strings sounds like skimpy underwear, but a violin has a G string; the other meaning is a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a violinist, who plays a G string, and also a cheat who embezzles small sums.

clue.text: Place underground to watch a Paxman grilling?

parts.note: to inter is to bury, putting a body underground
to view is to watch

explanation.surface: Asks where you might go below ground to watch Jeremy Paxman roasting a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Paxman was the famously aggressive BBC Newsnight presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paxman's hostile questioning of politicians on television is a broadcast interview.

clue.text: Ollie's negative HRT therapy

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: Ollie is the answer

parts.note: no is a negative reply

indicators.note: treatment changes the letters, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Ollie rejecting hormone replacement therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ollie is Oliver North, the US marine of the Iran-Contra scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieutenant Colonel Oliver North, central to the Iran-Contra affair, was nicknamed Ollie.

clue.text: Party's suppressing Prescott's last points

indicators.note: the parties hold the letter down inside them

parts.note: a do is a party, and the plural dos

indicators.note: Prescott's last means the final letter of his name

parts.note: the deputy prime minister's surname

explanation.surface: The Labour Party squashing John Prescott's final talking points.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was Labour's deputy prime minister in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Small round points are dots, as in a printed full stop.

clue.text: Some idiot in South-West Water?

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used
the answer sits inside the words of the water company's name

parts.note: the name of the water utility serving Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: Wonders whether some fool works at the regional water company.
explanation.walkthrough: South West Water is the utility serving Devon and Cornwall, often in the news for failures; the answer spans the join of its last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Twat is vulgar British slang for a stupid or obnoxious person, a cruder synonym of fool.

clue.text: Carrots give Brown one form of BSE

parts.note: BR is a standard abbreviation for brown
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a form of the letters is a rearrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Carrots giving Gordon Brown a kind of mad cow disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was then Chancellor. Carrots here are incentives, as in carrot and stick, not vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Inducements offered to persuade someone are carrots, and corrupt ones are bribes.

clue.text: Top pair of Nigella Lawson unsettled a Tory graph columnist

definitions.note: the Torygraph is Private Eye's name for the Conservative-leaning Daily Telegraph

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed and reordered

parts.note: the first two letters of Nigella
taken as written

explanation.surface: A leering line about the TV cook Nigella Lawson's top half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top pair' is a crude bust joke; it only means the first two letters of her first name. A N Wilson wrote a Telegraph column.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer A N Wilson was a regular Daily Telegraph columnist, the paper the Eye mocks as the Torygraph.

clue.text: Elegant note, the sound of one who's pissed

parts.note: C is a note of the musical scale

parts.words: the sound of one who's pissed
parts.note: hic is the hiccup of a drunk person; pissed is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A stylish musical note mistaken for a drunk's hiccup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, a synonym of elegant.

clue.text: Mean, pissed rat died

parts.note: tight and pissed are both British slang for drunk
a rat and an arse are both insults for a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A stingy drunk compared to a dead rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed rat' suggests the slang rat-arsed, meaning very drunk, but the pieces split differently. D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight-arsed is British slang for stingy with money, so it is a synonym of mean.
